target: Rwyt ti wedi dod mor bell, paid â stopio nawr.
english: You've come so far, don't stop now.
tip: paid â plus a verb-noun tells one person not to do something: paid â stopio, don't stop.

target: Po fwyaf dw i'n dysgu, po fwyaf dw i'n deall.
english: The more I learn, the more I understand.
tip: Po fwyaf...po fwyaf frames the more...the more: Po fwyaf dw i'n dysgu, the more I learn.

target: Mae fy nhad-cu yn adrodd straeon am yr hen ddyddiau.
english: My grandfather tells stories about the old days.
tip: fy, my, nasal-mutates the next word: tad-cu turns into fy nhad-cu (t to nh).

target: Mae tosturi yn bwysicach na chyfoeth.
english: Compassion is more important than wealth.
tip: na, than, aspirate-mutates c, p and t: cyfoeth becomes na chyfoeth.

target: Mae'r cerddorion yn well na'r llynedd.
english: The musicians are better than last year.
tip: Better is the irregular gwell, not mwy da: yn well na'r llynedd, better than last year.

target: Mae'r mynydd yn uwch na'r bryn.
english: The mountain is higher than the hill.
tip: Higher is the irregular uwch, from uchel: yn uwch na'r bryn, higher than the hill.

target: Mae'r pentref yn dawelach na'r dref.
english: The village is quieter than the town.
tip: Add -ach for -er or more: tawel, quiet, becomes tawelach, softened to dawelach after yn.

target: Mae hi'n gyrru i Gaerfyrddin bob wythnos.
english: She drives to Carmarthen every week.
tip: i, to, softens place names: Caerfyrddin becomes i Gaerfyrddin (c to g).

target: Mae'r gêm gyfartal yn siomi'r ddau dîm.
english: The drawn game disappoints both teams.
tip: A feminine noun softens the adjective after it: gêm plus cyfartal gives gêm gyfartal.

target: Mae Cymru'n harddach na llawer o wledydd.
english: Wales is more beautiful than many countries.
tip: o, meaning of or from, softens the next word: gwledydd becomes o wledydd.

target: Yr Wyddfa yw'r mynydd uchaf yng Nghymru.
english: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.
tip: In Wales is yng Nghymru: yn shifts to yng and Cymru nasal-mutates to Nghymru.

target: Mae'r llyn yn ddyfnach nag oeddwn i'n meddwl.
english: The lake is deeper than I thought.
tip: na becomes nag before a vowel: ddyfnach nag oeddwn, deeper than I was.

target: Dyna'r fferm lle maen nhw'n gwneud y caws.
english: That's the farm where they make the cheese.
tip: lle links a place to a clause, meaning where: y fferm lle maen nhw'n gwneud, the farm where they make.

target: Pe bawn i'n ennill mwy, byddwn i'n teithio'r byd.
english: If I earned more, I would travel the world.
tip: Pe bawn i means if I were: Pe bawn i'n ennill mwy, if I earned more.

target: Pryd mae'r dydd byrraf yn y flwyddyn?
english: When is the shortest day of the year?
tip: Add -af for the most: byr, short, becomes byrraf, shortest, doubling the r.

target: Pe bai band eang gwell gyda ni, byddwn i'n gweithio o gartref.
english: If we had better broadband, I'd work from home.
tip: Adjectives follow the noun in Welsh: band eang gwell reads broadband better, meaning better broadband.

target: Pe bai mwy o amser gyda fi, byddwn i'n dysgu chwarae'r delyn.
english: If I had more time, I would learn to play the harp.
tip: Pe bai sets up an unreal if, answered by byddwn i'n, I would: Pe bai mwy o amser..., byddwn i'n dysgu.

target: Dyma'r ffilm waethaf erioed.
english: This is the worst film ever.
tip: Bad has an irregular superlative: drwg becomes gwaethaf, worst, softened to ffilm waethaf here.

target: Mae Tom Jones yn ganwr enwog.
english: Tom Jones is a famous singer.
tip: Linking yn softens a following noun too: canwr becomes yn ganwr, a singer (c to g).

target: Mae fy mrawd yn hŷn na fi.
english: My brother is older than me.
tip: Older is the irregular hŷn, from hen: fy mrawd yn hŷn na fi, my brother is older than me.

target: Mae'r triongl hafalochrog yn cael tair ochr gyfartal.
english: The equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
tip: Three shows gender: tair with feminine nouns, tri with masculine. Here tair ochr, three sides.

target: Mae'r siart yn dangos y caneuon mwyaf poblogaidd.
english: The chart shows the most popular songs.
tip: For longer adjectives use mwyaf before the word instead of an -af ending: mwyaf poblogaidd, most popular.

target: Mae gofal plant fforddiadwy yn flaenoriaeth i rieni sy'n gweithio.
english: Affordable childcare is a priority for working parents.
tip: sy'n means who or that is, joining a doer to an action: rieni sy'n gweithio, parents who work.

target: Ein gwyliau oedd y gorau rydyn ni erioed wedi'u cael.
english: Our holiday was the best we've ever had.
tip: Best is the irregular superlative gorau, from da, never daaf: y gorau, the best.

target: Mae'n ymddangos bod pethau'n newid er gwell yn y gymuned leol.
english: It appears that things are changing for the better in the local community.
tip: bod means that after verbs of saying or seeming: Mae'n ymddangos bod pethau'n newid, it seems things change.

target: Pe bai mwy o adnoddau wedi'u dyrannu, gallai'r canlyniad fod wedi bod yn wahanol.
english: If more resources had been allocated, the outcome might have been different.
tip: A past unreal if adds wedi: Pe bai mwy o adnoddau wedi'u dyrannu, if more had been allocated, not were.

target: Mae fy nghoesau'n brifo.
english: My legs hurt.
tip: fy (my) triggers a nasal change: coesau turns into fy nghoesau (my legs), c becoming ngh.

target: Hedfanodd hi i Ffrainc.
english: She flew to France.
tip: The -odd ending marks a he/she past tense: hedfan (to fly) becomes Hedfanodd (flew).

target: Teithiais i drwy Gymru.
english: I travelled through Wales.
tip: drwy (through) softens the next word: Cymru becomes drwy Gymru, c changing to g.

target: Roedd fy nhad-cu'n adrodd straeon.
english: My grandfather was telling stories.
tip: After fy (my) the next word nasal-mutates: tad becomes fy nhad-cu here, t shifting to nh.
